I got an Arizer Air and I can't recommend vaping enough, especially if you're a daily user who still has a bunch of other stuff to do. I'll start off by answering your last question: I don't get 0-to-60 blazed as quickly as I do if I smoke, but I actually really prefer it that way. Well, there's always an MFLB. They're cheap, have simple construction so they're pretty difficult to break, and even if you do, the company stands behind its product so much that you can send them a broken one and they'll just replace it. Once you buy an MFLB, the company guarantees it forever... So basically guaranteed until the company goes out of business or you die. The downsides are that getting a good pull off of one is kind of an artform and it's something you probably won't be able to do perfectly right away, and that they use special (kinda expensive) batteries that stop holding very good charges kinda fast. You'll be charging the battery a TON.

Then there's a Pax. They're really spiffy looking and are a bit more advanced, mechanics-wise. They have more moving parts, which makes them more likely to have something on them break and also makes them harder to clean. However, you can actually control how hot you want it to get, and it has an indicator that tells you when it's at the perfect temperature to pull from, when it's getting too hot (pull more!) or when it's getting too cool (wait a bit). Pulls from a Pax are easy - there's no trick or technique to it like there is with an MFLB, and a Pax can hit for a lot longer at once.

They're both pretty small... Somewhere around lighter-sized. MFLBs you can get for about 100 bucks, though I'm not sure exactly what their base price is now. A Pax is more - about $200 - and are only sold by licensed vendors. If you can afford the extra 80 bucks, I'd say get a Pax.
